datasets: High School Dropout/Withdrawal Rate - City (BNIA Vital Signs via Open Baltimore, 1 citywide row)
BPD CompStat district figures week ending 2021-07-17 (hand-transcribed from PDF, not Open Baltimore)
concurrency_primitives: sync.WaitGroup + 1-slot buffered error channel in a custom group helper (concurrent.go); 2 goroutines load the two CSVs (main.go:261-272), 3 goroutines write the three outputs (main.go:281-287); no worker pool, no parallel parse/join/aggregate
design_patterns: Implicit two-stage pipeline (load -> write); errgroup-style helper; no named pattern claimed or realized
questions: Descriptive: how much gun violence is there, and how high is the dropout rate?
Exploratory: what patterns show up (district change 2020->2021, arrests per incident, dropout year-over-year)?
Explanatory: what correlates with a district's gun-related incidents?
Evaluative: did more gun arrests go with fewer gun incidents?
Predictive: can a district's 2020 gun incidents predict its 2021 count (leave-one-out)?
overview: Idiomatic, well-commented single-package Go split cleanly into ingest/validate, analysis, stats, HTML report and a small concurrency helper, with strong unit and end-to-end tests, deterministic atomic output and rigorous statistics (p-values, Spearman, leave-one-out). Highly maintainable and honest about limitations, but engineered around ~20 input numbers.
stakeholder_value: No stakeholder is named and the two datasets cannot be joined (one citywide dropout row vs nine police districts), so the report offers no cross-dataset insight; Q3-Q5 are CompStat-only and could be read off the source PDF. The statistical caveats are sound but a Mayor's Office would learn nothing actionable.
issues: Only one dataset is from Open Baltimore and it is a single aggregated citywide row; CompStat table is hand-typed from a BPD PDF
Datasets are never joined; cross-dataset requirement unmet by construction
Token concurrency: 2 loader + 3 writer goroutines, no worker pool or parallel aggregation
Shipped prebuilt binary is a Linux x86-64 ELF, not runnable on macOS
rationale: Full marks for build, run and README because everything works exactly as documented and is race-clean and tested. Heavy deductions on real_data (one tiny portal indicator plus a hand-transcribed PDF table, no join), concurrency (token), and stakeholder (no named stakeholders, no cross-dataset answers) because the core requirements of the assignment are not met despite the high code quality. Total 62, D.
